strengths: Novel frequency-domain perspective on gating mechanisms motivated by the convolution theorem
Comprehensive empirical validation across multiple architectures (ResNet18, MobileNetV2, EfficientFormer-v2) with detailed frequency decomposition analysis
Competitive ImageNet-1K results without advanced training techniques (distillation, re-parameterization), demonstrating practical value
Thorough ablation studies on activation functions and GLU designs (Tables 3, 5) that support theoretical insights
Well-documented experimental details, hyperparameters, and reproducibility information for full implementation
Honest discussion of limitations regarding high-frequency imperceptibility and scope constraints
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: Theorems 1-2 are well-known classical results from signal processing; the gap between mathematical properties and actual network learning dynamics is underexplored and not rigorously established
Causal claims lack rigorous support: evidence is primarily correlational (high accuracy on frequency subsets); alternative explanations like increased model expressiveness are not ruled out

Questionable practical relevance: paper admits very high-frequency components (r > 36) are 'nearly imperceptible to human eye' and networks 'face challenges' classifying them, undermining the central motivation

Insufficient statistical rigor: Table 2 reports single accuracy numbers without confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests despite claiming averaging over runs; improvements often <1% in magnitude

Artificial frequency decomposition: Fourier threshold-based partitioning (Eq. 1) may not align with how networks actually partition information; choice of different thresholds per-model (Section 3) suggests methodology may not capture fundamental properties

Limited evaluation scope: primarily ImageNet-1K classification only; detection/segmentation results relegated to supplementary material; no evaluation on non-vision tasks despite motivation from sequence processing
Incremental architectural contribution: GmNet is a standard efficient CNN with GLU blocks; novelty primarily in motivation rather than design; typical performance improvements are 1-2% over baselines

Incomplete justification of design choices: why ReLU6 specifically beyond empirical performance; 7×7 convolutions appear arbitrary; limited ablation on these components; insufficient discussion of why other efficient model designers haven't pursued high-frequency learning

strengths: Novel frequency-domain perspective on gating mechanisms with systematic analysis of how element-wise multiplication and activation functions shape frequency response
Strong practical results: GmNet achieves 79.3% ImageNet-1K with competitive latency, outperforming several baselines (4x faster than EfficientFormer-L1) without advanced training techniques
Comprehensive experimental validation with thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-5) examining activation functions, GLU designs, and architectural components across multiple architectures
Excellent visualization and clear presentation of frequency learning dynamics (Figures 3-4) with supporting evidence including kernel bandwidth analysis
Solid experimental methodology with good coverage of design choices and validation across different model sizes and configurations
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: Theorems 1-2 and Lemma 3 are well-established mathematical results; application to GLUs is straightforward without deep new insights into actual training dynamics

Weak connection between theory and architecture design: GmNet's specific choices (7×7 kernels, placement, ratio parameters) are not directly justified by the frequency analysis; architecture appears incremental relative to existing efficient models
Narrow evaluation scope: Limited to ImageNet-1K for main results; no evaluation on domains where GLUs are heavily used (NLP/sequences); no testing on larger models to establish applicability bounds

Crude frequency decomposition methodology using simple radius-based thresholding, with relatively small performance differences between variants; very high-frequency components are imperceptible to humans, raising questions about their relevance

Unexplained paradoxes in results: ReLU6 performs worse on low-frequencies but better overall (Table 3), suggesting the frequency-performance relationship is more nuanced than presented; different radius settings across model comparisons hinder direct comparison

Gap between claimed insights and design justification: Theorem 1 applies to any element-wise product, not specifically GLUs; paper doesn't rigorously prove GmNet's design follows from frequency insights rather than trial-and-error optimization

strengths: Novel frequency-domain perspective on GLUs with clear convolution theorem motivation
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple architectures (ResNet18, MobileNetV2, EfficientFormer-V2) with extensive ablations
Strong empirical results achieving SOTA for efficient models (GmNet-S3: 79.3%, GmNet-S4: 81.5%) with significant latency improvements
Systematic analysis of activation function smoothness effects on spectral learning with bandwidth analysis supporting claims
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, pseudocode, and promise to release code
Thorough downstream task validation including detection, segmentation, and domain-specific benchmarks
weaknesses: Theoretical analysis lacks rigor: Section 3.2 on activation smoothness describes function properties rather than establishing causality for network learning behavior
Frequency decomposition methodology is simplistic (hard radial threshold) and highly sensitive to threshold r choice; unclear how practitioners should select r
Evaluation on frequency-decomposed images is artificial and connection to full-image performance is not mechanistically established
Architectural design appears engineered rather than principled from frequency theory—hyperparameters (7×7 kernels, expansion ratios) not justified by frequency analysis
Significant adversarial robustness trade-off (~1% PGD accuracy drop for ReLU-based GLU) relegated to appendix without adequate discussion
Generalization concerns: ConvNeXt shows much smaller gains (+0.5%); large model behavior and Vision Transformer applicability unexplored
Limited engagement with prior spectral bias mitigation methods and incomplete comparison with related gating-based approaches (e.g., StarNet)
Critical ablations missing: kernel size sensitivity, systematic expansion ratio studies, error bars on main results beyond Table 5

strengths: Novel frequency-domain perspective on GLUs grounded in convolution theorem, providing new lens for understanding gating mechanisms' effect on spectral learning

Comprehensive experimental validation including extensive ablation studies across multiple backbones, frequency decomposition analysis, and downstream task evaluation with detailed reproducibility information
Strong empirical results with competitive efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs (GmNet-S3: 79.3% with 7.8M params, 1.2G FLOPs) and consistent improvements across model scales
Practical and simple architecture design that achieves results without complex training strategies, NAS, or distillation, with thorough implementation details
Clear problem motivation and intuitive exposition (particularly Figure 1) of how GLUs affect frequency learning in lightweight networks
weaknesses: Theoretical analysis lacks rigor: claims about activation smoothness and frequency characteristics rely on isolated Fourier properties rather than formal justification for why these transfer to learned representations in deep networks

Frequency decomposition methodology is simplistic (radial masking) with an arbitrary critical hyperparameter (radius r); Appendix A.11 reveals significant sensitivity where results become 'less pronounced' with different interval choices
Overstated claims about 'state-of-the-art': GmNet-S3 (79.3%) falls below LeViT-256 (81.5%), and GmNet-S4 is not substantially different in scale; comparison baseline definition is inconsistent

Limited architectural novelty: the proposed σ(x)·x design is extremely simple and well-established; GLUs are known; contribution is primarily analytical rather than architectural, with comparisons to concurrent gating methods (StarNet) remaining limited

Robustness-accuracy tradeoff inadequately addressed: Appendix A.7 shows ~1% PGD accuracy drop for high-frequency-emphasizing models; this vulnerability deserves main-paper discussion given on-device applications context
Generalization concerns: ConvNeXt experiments show smaller improvements (+0.5%) for larger models; paper acknowledges 'block design should be architecture-dependent,' limiting broader applicability
Design choices not fully explained: why σ(x)·x is optimal and why ReLU6 specifically are supported empirically but lack principled justification; post-hoc interpretation of experimental results

Experimental limitations: Table 3 shows selective frequency component comparisons with variable results across radii; mobile latency claims not fully supported (GmNet-S3 at 1.3ms not always fastest); all experiments at 224×224 resolution
